data.name: WinProcessOSQuery

data.description: This lookup table captures Windows Processes and ports they listen on. The population of this table requires running Windows osquery windows_processes_and_listening_ports via FortiSIEM Agent

data.description: This lookup table captures Windows services and the path from which they are launched. The population of this table requires running Windows osquery windows_services_running_stopped via FortiSIEM Agent.

data.description: This lookup table captures Windows Startup Programs. The population of this table requires running Windows osquery windows_startup_programs via FortiSIEM Agent.
data.name: WinStartupProgram

data.description: This lookup table captures users and the Windows hosts they login to via RDP. The population of this table requires running Windows Security event logs collected via OMI or FortiSIEM Agent

data.description: This lookup table captures user, Linux host they login to. The population of this table requires running Linux authentication logs collected via syslog.
data.name: LinuxSSHLogin

data.description: This lookup table captures functions of Unix binaries that can be used to bypass security restrictions, by breaking out of restricted shells, escalate privileges, maintain elevated privileges, spawn reverse shells and do other post-exploitation persistence tasks. This table can be populated by downloading a CSV file with matching fields from the GTFOBins project.
data.name: GTFOBin

data.description: This lookup table contains Active Directory techniques, commands, and functions that can be used natively to support offensive security operations and Red Team exercises. This table can be populated by downloading a CSV file with matching fields from the LOLAD project https://lolad-project.github.io/
data.name: LOLAD

data.description: This lookup table captures Living Off The Land Binaries, Scripts and Libraries (LOLBAS). These are trusted tools and local to Windows OS, but have been utilized by cyber attackers to bypass detection and hide malicious activity. This table can be populated by downloading a CSV file with the matching fields from the LOLBAS project: https://lolbas-project.github.io/api/
data.name: LOLBAS

data.description: This lookup table captures Living Off Trusted Sites (LOTS). These are legitimate domains that have been used by attackers for conducting phishing, command and control, exfiltration and tool download, to bypass detection and hide malicious activity. This table can be populated by downloading a CSV file with matching fields from the LOTS project: https://lots-project.com/
data.name: LOTS

data.description: This lookup table captures malicious powershelgl cmdlets that have been known to be used by attack frameworks.
data.name: MaliciousPowershellCmdlet
